preamble.title: Preamble to the Constitution of India
preamble.verbatim_text: WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and to secure to all its citizens: JUSTICE, social, economic and political; LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation; IN OUR CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949, do HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION.
preamble.plain_explanation: The Preamble embodies the foundational values, philosophy, and sovereign resolve of the Indian Republic. It is an integral, inviolable part of the Basic Structure of the Constitution.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: The Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution and can be amended under Article 368 without altering the Basic Structure.

landmark_precedents.case_title: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Secularism, federalism, and democracy in the Preamble are essential features of the basic structure.

schedules.title: Allocation of Seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)
schedules.summary: Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to States and Union Territories according to demographic representation.

schedules.title: Provisions as to Administration and Control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes
schedules.summary: Governance of Scheduled Areas in mainland States; Governor powers and Tribes Advisory Councils (Samatha v. State of A.P.).

schedules.title: Administration of Tribal Areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
schedules.summary: Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) and Regional Councils with legislative, judicial, and executive powers in North-Eastern tribal areas.

schedules.summary: Distribution of legislative competencies: List I (Union List - 97 items: Defence, Foreign Affairs, Currency), List II (State List - 66 items: Public Order, Police, Health), List III (Concurrent List - 47 items: Criminal Law, Contracts, Civil Procedure).

schedules.title: Recognised Languages of India
schedules.summary: Lists the 22 official languages of India (Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu).

schedules.title: Validation of Certain Acts and Regulations (Article 31B Immunity)

schedules.title: Provisions as to Disqualification on Ground of Defection
schedules.summary: Anti-defection law for legislators; disqualification on voluntary relinquishment of membership or defying party whip (Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu 1992 Supp (2) SCC 651).

schedules.title: Powers, Authority and Responsibilities of Panchayats
schedules.summary: Specifies 29 functional items devolved to rural local self-governments (Agriculture, Land improvement, Minor irrigation, Drinking water, Roads).

schedules.title: Powers, Authority and Responsibilities of Municipalities
schedules.summary: Specifies 18 functional items devolved to urban local bodies (Urban planning, Regulation of land use, Roads and bridges, Water supply, Public health).

articles.heading: Name and territory of the Union
articles.verbatim_text: (1) India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States. (2) The States and the territories thereof shall be as specified in the First Schedule. (3) The territory of India shall comprise: (a) the territories of the States; (b) the Union territories specified in the First Schedule; and (c) such other territories as may be acquired.
articles.plain_explanation: Establishes India (Bharat) as an indestructible Union of destructible States.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 1.
citizen_actionable_rights: Inherent right to all benefits of Indian Union territory without inter-State discrimination.

articles.heading: Admission or establishment of new States
articles.verbatim_text: Parliament may by law admit into the Union, or establish, new States on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.
articles.plain_explanation: Empowers Parliament to admit or establish new States from outside existing territory.
applicable_doctrines: Parliamentary Constituent Supremacy in Admission of External Territory
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 2.

articles.heading: Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States
articles.verbatim_text: Parliament may by law: (a) form a new State by separation of territory from any State or by uniting two or more States; (b) increase the area of any State; (c) diminish the area of any State; (d) alter the boundaries of any State; (e) alter the name of any State, provided that a Bill for the purpose is introduced only on President's recommendation and State Legislature views are sought.
articles.plain_explanation: Permits Parliament to reorganise States, alter boundaries, and rename States without mandatory concurrence of the State legislature.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Babulal Parate v. State of Bombay
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: State Legislature views under Article 3 proviso are advisory and do not bind Parliament.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 3.

articles.heading: Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 to provide for the amendment of the First and the Fourth Schedules
articles.verbatim_text: Laws reorganising States under Articles 2 and 3 do not constitute constitutional amendments under Article 368 and can be passed by simple majority.
articles.plain_explanation: Allows State reorganisation to proceed by ordinary legislation without the special majority of Article 368.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 4.

articles.heading: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
articles.verbatim_text: At the commencement of this Constitution every person who has his domicile in the territory of India and was born in India or either parents born in India or ordinarily resident for not less than five years shall be a citizen.
articles.plain_explanation: Grants citizenship to all persons domiciled in India at commencement (26 Jan 1950).
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 5.

articles.heading: Rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan
articles.verbatim_text: Citizenship rights for persons migrating from Pakistan to India prior to or post 19th July 1948 subject to registration.
articles.plain_explanation: Governs citizenship entitlement of partition refugees migrating into India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 6.

articles.heading: Rights of citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan
articles.verbatim_text: Deems persons migrating to Pakistan after 1st March 1947 to have forfeited Indian citizenship unless returned under resettlement permits.
articles.plain_explanation: Extinguishes citizenship upon migration to Pakistan after 1 March 1947.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 7.

articles.heading: Rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India
articles.verbatim_text: Provides for Indian diplomatic registration of persons of Indian origin residing abroad as citizens.
articles.plain_explanation: Facilitates diplomatic citizenship registration for overseas Indians.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 8.

articles.heading: Persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State not to be citizens
articles.verbatim_text: No person shall be a citizen of India if he has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of any foreign State.
articles.plain_explanation: Mandates strict single citizenship; Indian citizenship automatically terminates on acquiring foreign nationality.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 9.

articles.heading: Continuance of the rights of citizenship
articles.verbatim_text: Every person who is a citizen under this Part shall continue to be such citizen, subject to laws made by Parliament.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees that citizenship cannot be arbitrarily revoked except pursuant to parliamentary enactment.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 10.

articles.heading: Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law
articles.verbatim_text: Parliament has complete plenary power to make provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all matters relating thereto.
articles.plain_explanation: Confers absolute plenary power on Parliament to legislate on citizenship (e.g., Citizenship Act, 1955).
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 11.

articles.heading: Definition of State for Fundamental Rights Enforcement
articles.verbatim_text: In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires, 'the State' includes the Government and Parliament of India and the Government and the Legislature of each of the States and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.
articles.plain_explanation: Defines which authorities are bound by Fundamental Rights and amenable to writ jurisdiction under Article 32 and Article 226.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib Sehravardi
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: A corporation or society is 'State' under Art 12 if State has deep and pervasive financial, functional, and administrative control.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Six-Factor Test for Instrumentality of State

landmark_precedents.case_title: Zee Telefilms Ltd. v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: BCCI is not State under Article 12 as it lacks state monopoly and state financial funding, though amenable to Article 226 for public functions.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Distinction between Article 12 State and Article 226 Public Duty

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Frame respondent as 'State' by pleading deep and pervasive government financial aid, functional monopoly, and statutory control under Ajay Hasia tests.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to hold every government department, municipal corporation, and PSU accountable for fundamental rights violations.

articles.heading: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights
articles.verbatim_text: (1) All laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution, in so far as they are inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void. (2) The State shall not make any law which takes away or abridges the rights conferred by this Part and any law made in contravention of this clause shall, to the extent of the contravention, be void. (3) 'Law' includes Ordinance, order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification, custom having the force of law.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees judicial review; renders any pre-constitutional or post-constitutional statute, rule, ordinance, or administrative order void if it violates Fundamental Rights.

landmark_precedents.case_title: State of West Bengal v. Committee for Protection of Democratic Rights
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Power of judicial review under Articles 13, 32, and 226 is an integral part of the basic structure.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of M.P.
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Pre-constitutional laws violating fundamental rights are not dead; they remain dormant under an eclipse and revive if constitutional impediment is lifted.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Directly seek declaration that the impugned enactment, notification, or executive order is ultra vires Article 13(2) read with Part III.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to challenge unconstitutional executive orders, bylaws, and police notifications before High Courts or Supreme Court.

articles.heading: Equality before law and equal protection of the laws
articles.verbatim_text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees universal equality, forbids arbitrary state action, and mandates reasonable classification based on intelligible differentia with rational nexus.

landmark_precedents.case_title: E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Equality is dynamic; arbitrariness and equality are sworn enemies. State action that is arbitrary violates Article 14.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Legislation can be struck down for 'manifest arbitrariness' if it is irrational, capricious, or lacks an adequate determining principle.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Manifest Arbitrariness as a Ground to Strike Down Plenary Legislation

concordance_links.notes: Civil remedies enforcing equal treatment and declaring discriminatory state orders void.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Pleaded in every writ petition: establish either (a) unequal treatment among equals without intelligible differentia, or (b) patent manifest arbitrariness / caprice in State action.
citizen_actionable_rights: Absolute immunity from capricious, whimsical, or discriminatory government action.

articles.heading: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
articles.verbatim_text: (1) The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them. (2) No citizen shall be subject to disability/restriction regarding access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, public entertainment, or wells/tanks/bathing ghats. Special provisions for women, children (cl. 3), backward classes (cl. 4, 5), and EWS (cl. 6) are protected.
articles.plain_explanation: Prohibits discrimination on 5 specific grounds against citizens, guarantees horizontal equality in public places, and authorizes affirmative action.
reasonable_restrictions: Protective discrimination for women and children (15(3))
applicable_doctrines: Horizontal Rights Application in Public Facilities

landmark_precedents.case_title: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: 103rd Constitutional Amendment providing 10% EWS reservation does not violate the Basic Structure.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 15.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to unhindered access to commercial establishments, public wells, schools, and spaces without caste/religion discrimination.

articles.heading: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
articles.verbatim_text: (1) There shall be equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State. (2) No citizen shall be ineligible or discriminated against on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence. Clauses (4), (4A), (4B), and (6) safeguard affirmative action reservations.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees equal opportunity in government jobs while permitting affirmative action reservations for underrepresented classes.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Reservation under Article 16(4) capped at 50%; creamy layer must be excluded from OBC reservations.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 16.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to fair, non-discriminatory recruitment in public employment and transparent selection criteria.

articles.heading: Abolition of Untouchability
articles.verbatim_text: 'Untouchability' is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The enforcement of any disability arising out of 'Untouchability' shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.
articles.plain_explanation: Absolute fundamental right abolishing untouchability; enforceable horizontally against private individuals and State alike.

concordance_links.target_statute: Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 / SC & ST PoA Act, 1989
concordance_links.notes: Penal sanction for enforcing untouchability disabilities.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 17.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to dignity and total protection against social boycott, untouchability, or caste-based exclusion.

articles.heading: Abolition of titles
articles.verbatim_text: (1) No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State. (2) No citizen shall accept any title from any foreign State.
articles.plain_explanation: Abolishes hereditary aristocratic titles to foster a democratic and egalitarian society (National Awards like Bharat Ratna upheld as decorations, not titles).
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 18.

articles.heading: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
articles.verbatim_text: (1) All citizens shall have the right: (a) to freedom of speech and expression; (b) to assemble peaceably and without arms; (c) to form associations or unions or co-operative societies; (d) to move freely throughout the territory of India; (e) to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India; and (g) to practise any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade or business. Clauses (2) to (6) prescribe exhaustive reasonable restrictions.
articles.plain_explanation: The bedrock charter of civil liberties: speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession, protected against disproportionate State restriction.
reasonable_restrictions: Article 19(2): Sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to an offence.
Article 19(6): General public interests, professional or technical qualifications, State carrying on trade/monopoly.
applicable_doctrines: Horizontal Application against Non-State Entities (Kaushal Kishore)

landmark_precedents.case_title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Section 66A IT Act struck down as unconstitutional for overbreadth and chilling free speech under Article 19(1)(a).
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Overbreadth & Chilling Effect on Internet Speech

landmark_precedents.case_title: Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Freedom of speech and freedom to carry on business using the internet are constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g); internet shutdowns subject to proportionality.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Internet Freedom as Fundamental Right & Proportionality Test

landmark_precedents.case_title: Kaushal Kishore v. State of U.P.
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: A fundamental right under Article 19 and 21 can be enforced even against persons other than the State or its instrumentalities.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Horizontal Direct Enforcement of Articles 19 & 21 against Private Individuals

concordance_links.notes: Penal provisions on speech (defamation/public mischief) must satisfy Article 19(2) scrutiny.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Challenge speech muzzling, trade bans, and unreasonable administrative conditions by showing that the restriction fails the four-pronged Modern Proportionality Test.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to speak, criticize government policies, report facts online, peaceful protest, and carry on legal business without arbitrary police interference.

articles.heading: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
articles.verbatim_text: (1) No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act, nor subjected to a greater penalty (Ex-post facto prohibition). (2) No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once (Double jeopardy). (3) No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself (Self-incrimination).
articles.plain_explanation: Provides 3 absolute criminal justice safeguards: immunity from retroactive penal laws, protection against double jeopardy, and absolute right against self-incrimination.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Selvi v. State of Karnataka
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Involuntary narco-analysis, polygraph (lie-detector), and Brain Electrical Activation Profile (BEAP) tests violate Article 20(3) and are unconstitutional.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Rao Shiv Bahadur Singh v. State of V.P.
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Article 20(1) prohibits both retroactive criminalisation and retroactive enhancement of punishments.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Absolute Prohibition of Retroactive Penal Statutes

concordance_links.notes: Autrefois acquit / convict and witness interrogation safeguards.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Invoke Article 20(3) in bail and quashing petitions whenever police attempt forced confessions, involuntary narco tests, or coercive disclosure.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to absolute silence in police custody, immunity from retroactive penal charges, and protection against multiple prosecutions for one incident.

articles.heading: Protection of life and personal liberty
articles.verbatim_text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
articles.plain_explanation: The crown jewel of Indian constitutional jurisprudence: life with human dignity, personal liberty, bodily autonomy, privacy, right to health, speedy trial, and fair procedure.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Procedure established by law depriving liberty must be 'just, fair, and reasonable'—not fanciful, oppressive, or arbitrary. Interlinks Articles 14, 19, and 21.

landmark_precedents.case_title: K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Right to privacy is an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21; State infringement requires legitimate aim, statutory backing, proportionality, and procedural safeguards.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Constitutional Right to Privacy & Modern Proportionality Test

landmark_precedents.case_title: Common Cause (A Regd. Society) v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Right to life with dignity includes the right to die with dignity; executed Living Wills / Advance Medical Directives for passive euthanasia recognized.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Right to Die with Dignity & Passive Euthanasia

concordance_links.notes: Arrest guidelines and statutory default bail grounded directly in Article 21 liberty.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Primary constitutional grounding for all bail, quashing, habeas corpus, medical negligence, privacy violations, and police brutality matters.
citizen_actionable_rights: Inviolable right to life, dignity, informational privacy, medical treatment, clean drinking water, legal aid, and freedom from unlawful detention.

articles.heading: Right to education
articles.verbatim_text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees free and compulsory elementary education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. UOI
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: 25% quota in private unaided schools under RTE Act constitutionally valid under Article 21A.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Affirmative Action in Primary School Admissions

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 21A.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right of every child aged 6-14 to free admission, books, and schooling in government or quota private schools.

articles.heading: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
articles.verbatim_text: (1) No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice. (2) Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest excluding the time necessary for the journey. Clauses (4) to (7) govern preventive detention.
articles.plain_explanation: Prescribes mandatory constitutional arrest safeguards: communication of grounds of arrest, right to counsel, and mandatory 24-hour Magistrate production.

landmark_precedents.case_title: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Custodial violence violates Article 21; laid down 11 binding guidelines on arrest memos, family notification, medical inspection, and legal representation.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Mandatory Arrest Guidelines & Custodial Torture Remedies

landmark_precedents.case_title: Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Grounds of arrest must be furnished to the arrested person in writing without exception at the time of arrest under Article 22(1).

concordance_links.notes: Notice of appearance before arrest and 24-hour production before Judicial Magistrate.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Instantly seek Habeas Corpus or bail under Section 480 BNSS / 437 CrPC if grounds of arrest were not furnished in writing or production was delayed beyond 24 hours.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to demand written grounds of arrest, right to call family, right to consult lawyer immediately, and right to be brought before a Magistrate within 24 hours.

articles.heading: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
articles.verbatim_text: (1) Traffic in human beings and begar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law. (2) State may impose compulsory service for public purposes without discrimination.
articles.plain_explanation: Abolishes human trafficking, begar (unpaid servitude), and bonded labour; enforceable horizontally against private employers.

landmark_precedents.case_title: People's Union for Democratic Rights (Asiad Workers) v. UOI
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Payment of wages below the statutory minimum wage constitutes 'forced labour' under Article 23.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 23.
citizen_actionable_rights: Absolute right to receive statutory minimum wages; complete immunity from bonded labour or withholding of passport/papers.

articles.heading: Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.
articles.verbatim_text: No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment.
articles.plain_explanation: Total prohibition against employing children below 14 years in factories, mines, or hazardous occupations.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 24.

articles.heading: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
articles.verbatim_text: (1) Subject to public order, morality and health and to the other provisions of this Part, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion. (2) Authorizes State regulation of secular activities and social welfare/reform.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees individual freedom of conscience and religious practice, subject to public order, morality, health, and other fundamental rights.
reasonable_restrictions: Other provisions of Part III (Fundamental Rights prevail over religious practices)

landmark_precedents.case_title: Indian Young Lawyers Association (Sabarimala) v. State of Kerala
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Exclusion of women aged 10-50 from Sabarimala temple violates Article 14, 15, and 25(1); religious practice must conform to constitutional morality.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Constitutional Morality Prevails Over Discriminatory Religious Custom

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 25.
citizen_actionable_rights: Right to practice any faith, or no faith, in personal life without State coercion.

articles.heading: Freedom to manage religious affairs
articles.verbatim_text: Subject to public order, morality and health, every religious denomination or any section thereof shall have the right: (a) to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes; (b) to manage its own affairs in matters of religion; (c) to own and acquire movable and immovable property; and (d) to administer such property in accordance with law.
articles.plain_explanation: Grants collective religious denominations the right to manage their internal religious affairs and own property.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 26.

articles.heading: Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion
articles.verbatim_text: No person shall be compelled to pay any taxes, the proceeds of which are specifically appropriated in payment of expenses for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.
articles.plain_explanation: Strict prohibition against the State spending taxpayer funds to promote any specific religion; core secularism pillar.
applicable_doctrines: Strict Separation of Public Tax Revenue from Sectarian Endowments
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 27.

articles.heading: Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions
articles.verbatim_text: Prohibits compulsory religious instruction in wholly State-funded educational institutions and guarantees that no student in state-aided institutions can be compelled to attend religious worship.
articles.plain_explanation: Maintains neutrality of State schools by barring compelled religious indoctrination.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 28.

articles.heading: Protection of interests of minorities
articles.verbatim_text: (1) Any section of the citizens residing in the territory of India or any part thereof having a distinct language, script or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same. (2) No citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language or any of them.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees cultural and linguistic rights to all citizens and bars discrimination in state-funded educational institutions.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 29.

articles.heading: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
articles.verbatim_text: (1) All minorities, whether based on religion or language, shall have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. State aid shall not discriminate against minority-managed institutions.
articles.plain_explanation: Conveys special protection to religious and linguistic minorities to establish and run educational institutions without nationalisation or arbitrary interference.

landmark_precedents.case_title: T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Minority status is determined State-wise; unaided minority institutions have substantial autonomy in administration subject to academic standards.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: State-Wise Demarcation of Minority Status & Institutional Autonomy

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 30.

articles.heading: Compulsory acquisition of property (Repealed)
articles.verbatim_text: [Repealed by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, section 6 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979)]. Note: Right to property transitioned to Article 300A as a constitutional and human right.
articles.plain_explanation: Historical article repealed in 1978; property rights now protected under Article 300A.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 31.

articles.heading: Saving of laws providing for acquisition of estates, etc.
articles.verbatim_text: Shields laws providing for acquisition of estates, takeover of management of properties, or amalgamation of corporations from challenge under Articles 14 and 19.
articles.plain_explanation: Protects agrarian land reforms and corporate takeovers in public interest from constitutional challenge.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 31A.

articles.heading: Validation of certain Acts and Regulations
articles.verbatim_text: Provides blanket protection to Acts and Regulations specified in the Ninth Schedule against fundamental rights challenges, subject to the Basic Structure doctrine.
articles.plain_explanation: Ninth Schedule immunity mechanism; laws added after 24 April 1973 remain subject to judicial review for Basic Structure infringement.

landmark_precedents.case_title: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: All statutory amendments included in Ninth Schedule on or after 24 April 1973 are subject to judicial review; if they abrogate the basic structure, they will be struck down.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Dual Test of Basic Structure Review for Ninth Schedule Acts

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 31B.

articles.heading: Saving of laws giving effect to certain directive principles
articles.verbatim_text: Shields laws giving effect to the policy of the State towards securing Directive Principles in Article 39(b) and 39(c) from invalidation under Article 14 or Article 19.
articles.plain_explanation: Prioritizes distribution of material resources (Art 39(b)) and prevention of concentration of wealth (Art 39(c)) over private property claims.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: The Indian Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the balance between Parts III and IV. To give absolute primacy to one over the other is to disturb the harmony of the Constitution.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Harmonious Balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 31C.

articles.heading: Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part
articles.verbatim_text: (1) The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed. (2) The Supreme Court shall have power to issue directions or orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari. (3) Parliament may empower other courts. (4) The right guaranteed by this article shall not be suspended except as otherwise provided for by this Constitution.
articles.plain_explanation: The very soul of the Constitution (Dr. B.R. Ambedkar): an independent Fundamental Right to petition the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of any Fundamental Right via prerogative writs.
applicable_doctrines: Right to Constitutional Remedies as Inviolable Basic Structure

landmark_precedents.case_title: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Article 32 is not confined to traditional adversarial litigation; epistolary jurisdiction permits public-spirited citizens to move the Court on behalf of underprivileged persons whose rights are breached.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) Standing & Court Commissions

landmark_precedents.case_title: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak)
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Power of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is not only injunctive but remedial; Court can award exemplary damages and compensation for violation of fundamental rights.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Constitutional Tort & Remedial Compensation under Article 32

concordance_links.notes: Complementary writ jurisdiction of High Courts; High Court has wider scope encompassing legal rights.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Frame petition invoking specific prerogative writ: Habeas Corpus (illegal arrest), Mandamus (statutory failure), Quo Warranto (usurped public office), Certiorari (quashing quasi-judicial orders).
citizen_actionable_rights: Inviolable guaranteed right to approach the Supreme Court of India directly without exhausting intermediate appellate tiers whenever fundamental rights are infringed.

articles.heading: Power of Parliament to modify the rights conferred by this Part in their application to Forces, etc.
articles.verbatim_text: Empowers Parliament to restrict or abrogate fundamental rights for Armed Forces, Police Forces, and Intelligence agencies to ensure proper discharge of duties and maintenance of discipline.
articles.plain_explanation: Allows statutory limitation of fundamental rights for armed forces and police.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 33.

articles.heading: Restriction on rights conferred by this Part while martial law is in force in any area
articles.verbatim_text: Empowers Parliament to indemnify state officials for acts done in connection with the maintenance or restoration of order in areas under Martial Law.
articles.plain_explanation: Governs indemnity during martial law declarations.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 34.

articles.heading: Legislation to give effect to the provisions of this Part
articles.verbatim_text: Confers exclusive legislative power on Parliament (to the exclusion of State Legislatures) to prescribe punishments for offences declared under Part III (e.g., Articles 17 and 23).
articles.plain_explanation: Ensures nationwide uniformity in penal statutes enforcing Fundamental Rights.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 35.

articles.heading: Definition of State in Part IV
articles.verbatim_text: Same definition of State as Article 12 applies to Part IV.
articles.plain_explanation: Identifies authorities responsible for implementing Directive Principles.

articles.heading: Application of the principles contained in this Part
articles.verbatim_text: Provisions in Part IV shall not be enforceable by any court, but the principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
articles.plain_explanation: Directives are non-justiciable directly, but are foundational in interpreting fundamental rights and state laws.

articles.heading: State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people
articles.verbatim_text: State shall strive to promote welfare of the people by securing a social order in which justice, social, economic and political, informs all institutions, and minimize inequalities in income, status, and opportunities.
articles.plain_explanation: Mandates creation of a welfare state eliminating socio-economic inequalities.

articles.heading: Certain principles of policy to be followed by the State
articles.verbatim_text: Mandates adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of material resources (39(b)), prevention of concentration of wealth (39(c)), equal pay for equal work (39(d)), and protection of workers' and children's health (39(e), 39(f)).

articles.heading: Equal justice and free legal aid

articles.heading: Right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases
articles.verbatim_text: State shall, within limits of economic capacity, make effective provision for securing right to work, education, and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement.

articles.heading: Provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief

landmark_precedents.case_title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala

articles.heading: Promotion of co-operative societies
articles.verbatim_text: State shall endeavour to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control and professional management of co-operative societies.
articles.plain_explanation: Promotion of rural and urban cooperative movement (97th Amendment).

landmark_precedents.case_title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Fundamental rights and Directive Principles are complementary and supplementary to each other.

articles.heading: Uniform civil code for the citizens
articles.verbatim_text: The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India.
articles.plain_explanation: Directs State towards enacting common civil laws governing marriage, divorce, inheritance, and succession for all citizens regardless of religion.

articles.heading: Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years
articles.verbatim_text: The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
articles.plain_explanation: Directs state to fund preschool and anganwadi nutritional/educational care.

landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Fundamental rights and Directive Principles are complementary and supplementary to each other.

articles.heading: Promotion of educational and economic interests of SC, ST and other weaker sections
articles.verbatim_text: The State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, and shall protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.
articles.plain_explanation: Mandates state scholarships, welfare hostels, and economic development for SC/ST/OBC.

articles.heading: Duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health
articles.verbatim_text: State shall regard raising nutrition, standard of living, and improving public health as its primary duties, and endeavour to bring about prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs harmful to health.
articles.plain_explanation: Directs public healthcare investments, food security acts, and permits state liquor prohibition.

articles.verbatim_text: State shall endeavour to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and preserve/improve breeds and prohibit the slaughter of cows and calves and other milch and draught cattle.

articles.heading: Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wild life
articles.verbatim_text: The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wild life of the country.
articles.plain_explanation: Environmental charter directing State to combat pollution and protect wildlife (Wildlife Protection Act, EPA 1986).

articles.verbatim_text: Obligation of State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest declared of national importance from spoliation, destruction, or removal.
articles.plain_explanation: Mandates preservation of national heritage and historical monuments.

articles.verbatim_text: The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

articles.heading: Promotion of international peace and security
articles.verbatim_text: State shall endeavour to promote international peace, maintain just and honourable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.
articles.plain_explanation: Constitutional foundation of Indian foreign policy and treaty compliance.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Fundamental rights and Directive Principles are complementary and supplementary to each other.

articles.heading: Fundamental duties of every citizen of India
articles.verbatim_text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India: (a) to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals, the National Flag and National Anthem; (b) to cherish and follow noble ideals of national struggle; (c) to uphold sovereignty, unity and integrity of India; (d) to defend country; (e) to promote harmony and brotherhood transcending religious, linguistic, regional diversities and renounce practices derogatory to dignity of women; (f) to value composite culture; (g) to protect environment including forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife; (h) to develop scientific temper, humanism, spirit of inquiry and reform; (i) to safeguard public property and abjure violence; (j) to strive towards excellence in all spheres; (k) parent/guardian to provide education opportunities to child between 6 and 14 years.
articles.plain_explanation: Prescribes 11 moral, civic, and constitutional duties for every Indian citizen, functioning as an aid in interpreting statutory obligations and testing legislative reasonableness.
applicable_doctrines: Constitutional Duty as Reasonable Restriction Ground

landmark_precedents.case_title: AIIMS Students' Union v. AIIMS
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Fundamental duties under Article 51A are not useless; they can be used to interpret ambiguous statutes and uphold reasonable restrictions on fundamental rights.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 51A.

articles.heading: The President of India
articles.verbatim_text: There shall be a President of India.
articles.plain_explanation: Establishes the supreme executive constitutional head of the Republic of India.

articles.heading: Executive power of the Union
articles.verbatim_text: The executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with this Constitution; supreme command of the Defence Forces shall be vested in the President.
articles.plain_explanation: Vests union executive and military command in the President.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 53.

articles.heading: Election of President
articles.verbatim_text: Electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of Legislative Assemblies of the States.
articles.plain_explanation: Prescribes democratic composition of the presidential electoral college.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 54.

articles.heading: Manner of election of President
articles.verbatim_text: Proportional representation by means of single transferable vote and secret ballot ensuring parity between Union and States.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees federal parity in presidential voting weight.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 55.

articles.heading: Term of office of President
articles.verbatim_text: Five-year term from date of entering office, subject to resignation to VP or impeachment.
articles.plain_explanation: Prescribes 5-year presidential tenure.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 56.

articles.heading: Eligibility for re-election
articles.verbatim_text: A person who holds, or who has held, office as President shall be eligible for re-election.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 61.

articles.verbatim_text: President shall have the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence in all cases where sentence is by Court Martial or death sentence.

articles.heading: Sessions of Parliament, prorogation and dissolution

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 85.

articles.heading: Right of President to address and send messages to Houses
articles.verbatim_text: President may address either House or send messages.

articles.heading: Special address by the President
articles.verbatim_text: President addresses both Houses at commencement of first session after election and each year.
articles.plain_explanation: President's annual address.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 87.

articles.heading: Rights of Ministers and Attorney-General as respects Houses
articles.verbatim_text: Ministers and Attorney-General can speak and participate in proceedings without right to vote.
articles.plain_explanation: Ministers and AG rights in Parliament.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 88.

articles.heading: The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States
articles.verbatim_text: Vice-President is Chairman; Council elects Deputy Chairman.
articles.plain_explanation: Rajya Sabha presiding officers.

articles.heading: Vacation, resignation and removal of Deputy Chairman
articles.verbatim_text: Procedures for vacation or removal of Deputy Chairman.
articles.plain_explanation: Removal of Deputy Chairman.

articles.heading: Power of Deputy Chairman or other person to perform duties of Chairman
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 91 of the Constitution of India regarding Power of Deputy Chairman or other person to perform duties of Chairman.
articles.plain_explanation: Power of Deputy Chairman or other person to perform duties of Chairman under Part V of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 91.

articles.heading: Chairman or Deputy Chairman not to preside while resolution for removal is under consideration
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 92 of the Constitution of India regarding Chairman or Deputy Chairman not to preside while resolution for removal is under consideration.
articles.plain_explanation: Chairman or Deputy Chairman not to preside while resolution for removal is under consideration under Part V of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 92.

articles.heading: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People
articles.verbatim_text: Lok Sabha elects Speaker and Deputy Speaker from among its members.
articles.plain_explanation: Presiding officers of Lok Sabha.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 93.

articles.heading: Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker
articles.verbatim_text: Vacation, resignation, and 14-day notice removal resolution.
