articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 94.

articles.heading: Power of Deputy Speaker or other person to perform duties of Speaker
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 95 of the Constitution of India regarding Power of Deputy Speaker or other person to perform duties of Speaker.
articles.plain_explanation: Power of Deputy Speaker or other person to perform duties of Speaker under Part V of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 95.

articles.heading: Speaker or Deputy Speaker not to preside while resolution for removal is under consideration
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 96 of the Constitution of India regarding Speaker or Deputy Speaker not to preside while resolution for removal is under consideration.
articles.plain_explanation: Speaker or Deputy Speaker not to preside while resolution for removal is under consideration under Part V of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 96.

articles.heading: Salaries and allowances of Chairman, Deputy Chairman, Speaker and Deputy Speaker
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 97 of the Constitution of India regarding Salaries and allowances of Chairman, Deputy Chairman, Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
articles.plain_explanation: Salaries and allowances of Chairman, Deputy Chairman, Speaker and Deputy Speaker under Part V of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 97.

articles.heading: Secretariat of Parliament
articles.verbatim_text: Independent secretarial staff for each House of Parliament.
articles.plain_explanation: Parliamentary Secretariat autonomy.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 98.

articles.heading: Oath or affirmation by members
articles.verbatim_text: Every member must make oath before President or designee before taking seat.
articles.plain_explanation: Mandatory MP oath.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 99.

articles.heading: Voting in Houses, power of Houses to act notwithstanding vacancies and quorum
articles.verbatim_text: Decisions by majority; casting vote by Speaker; quorum is 1/10th of membership.
articles.plain_explanation: Parliamentary voting and quorum.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 100.

articles.heading: Vacation of seats
articles.verbatim_text: Prohibits double membership of both Houses or State Assembly; resignation; 60-day unexcused absence.
articles.plain_explanation: Vacation of Parliamentary seats.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 101.

articles.heading: Disqualifications for membership
articles.verbatim_text: Disqualified if holds office of profit, unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, not a citizen, or Tenth Schedule defection.
articles.plain_explanation: Grounds for disqualifying MPs.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 102.

articles.heading: Decision on questions as to disqualifications of members
articles.verbatim_text: President decides on advice of Election Commission; Tenth Schedule decided by Speaker.
articles.plain_explanation: Adjudication of MP disqualifications.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 103.

articles.heading: Penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation or when disqualified
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 104 of the Constitution of India regarding Penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation or when disqualified.
articles.plain_explanation: Penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation or when disqualified under Part V of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 104.

articles.heading: Powers, privileges, etc., of the Houses of Parliament and of the members
articles.verbatim_text: Freedom of speech in Parliament; no member shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said or any vote given by him in Parliament or any committee thereof.
articles.plain_explanation: Guarantees absolute legislative speech immunity; protects lawmakers from civil and criminal liability for parliamentary speeches/votes (Sita Soren [2024] INSC 167 - bribery not protected).

landmark_precedents.case_title: Sita Soren v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Parliamentary privilege under Article 105/194 does not protect legislators accepting bribes for speeches or votes.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 105.

articles.heading: Salaries and allowances of members
articles.verbatim_text: Salaries and pensions of MPs determined by law made by Parliament.
articles.plain_explanation: Parliamentary salaries.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 106.

articles.heading: Provisions as to introduction and passing of Bills
articles.verbatim_text: Bills may originate in either House; must be agreed to by both Houses.
articles.plain_explanation: Ordinary legislative procedure.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 107.

articles.heading: Joint sitting of both Houses in certain cases
articles.verbatim_text: President may summon joint sitting if Bill passed by one House is rejected by other or stalled 6 months.
articles.plain_explanation: Deadlock resolution via Joint Sitting.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 108.

articles.heading: Special procedure in respect of Money Bills
articles.verbatim_text: Money Bills cannot be introduced in Rajya Sabha; Rajya Sabha must return within 14 days.
articles.plain_explanation: Primacy of Lok Sabha in Money Bills.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 109.

articles.heading: Definition of 'Money Bills'
articles.verbatim_text: A Bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with imposition/regulation of taxes, borrowing, Consolidated Fund appropriations, etc. Speaker's decision thereon is final.
articles.plain_explanation: Strict constitutional definition of Money Bills bypassing Rajya Sabha veto; subject to judicial review if misused (Aadhaar Judgment).
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 110.

articles.heading: Assent to Bills
articles.verbatim_text: President declares assent, withholds assent, or returns non-Money Bill for reconsideration.
articles.plain_explanation: Presidential assent and suspensive veto.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 111.

articles.heading: Annual financial statement (Union Budget)
articles.verbatim_text: President shall in respect of every financial year cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure.
articles.plain_explanation: Mandates the presentation of the Union Budget before Parliament.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 112.

articles.heading: Procedure in Parliament with respect to estimates
articles.verbatim_text: Expenditure charged on Consolidated Fund not submitted to vote; other expenditure submitted as Demands for Grants.
articles.plain_explanation: Parliamentary budget voting.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 113.

articles.heading: Appropriation Bills
articles.verbatim_text: No money shall be withdrawn from Consolidated Fund of India except under appropriation made by law.
articles.plain_explanation: Appropriation Act mandate.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 114.

articles.heading: Supplementary, additional or excess grants
articles.verbatim_text: Provisions for supplementary grants when sanctioned amounts are insufficient.
articles.plain_explanation: Supplementary budget procedure.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 115.

articles.heading: Votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants
articles.verbatim_text: Advance grants made pending passage of Appropriation Bill.
articles.plain_explanation: Vote on Account procedure.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 116.

articles.heading: Special provisions as to financial Bills
articles.verbatim_text: Financial Bills introduced only on President's recommendation.
articles.plain_explanation: Financial bills procedure.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 117.

articles.heading: Rules of procedure
articles.verbatim_text: Each House of Parliament may make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
articles.plain_explanation: Parliamentary rulemaking power.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 118.

articles.heading: Regulation by law of procedure in Parliament in relation to financial business
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 119 of the Constitution of India regarding Regulation by law of procedure in Parliament in relation to financial business.
articles.plain_explanation: Regulation by law of procedure in Parliament in relation to financial business under Part V of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 119.

articles.heading: Language to be used in Parliament
articles.verbatim_text: Hindi or English; Presiding officer may permit mother tongue speech.
articles.plain_explanation: Language in parliamentary debates.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 120.

articles.heading: Restriction on discussion in Parliament
articles.verbatim_text: No discussion in Parliament regarding conduct of Supreme Court or High Court Judges in discharge of duties except on impeachment motion.
articles.plain_explanation: Protection of judicial independence from parliamentary criticism.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 121.

articles.heading: Courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament
articles.verbatim_text: Validity of parliamentary proceedings cannot be called into question on ground of alleged irregularity of procedure.
articles.plain_explanation: Parliamentary internal autonomy shield.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 122.

articles.chapter_title: Chapter III: Legislative Powers of the President
articles.heading: Power of President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament
articles.verbatim_text: (1) If at any time both Houses of Parliament are not in session, and President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action, he may promulgate such Ordinances as circumstances appear to him to require. Ceases to operate 6 weeks from reassembly of Parliament.
articles.plain_explanation: Emergency legislative power of executive; cannot be used to bypass legislative debate or re-promulgated endlessly without parliamentary ratification.

landmark_precedents.case_title: Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Re-promulgation of ordinances without placing them before the legislature is a fraud on the Constitution and subverts democratic governance.

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 123.

articles.heading: Establishment and constitution of Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: There shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice of India and other Judges. Judges appointed by President after consultation with Judges of Supreme Court (Collegium system). Impeachment requires address by each House supported by 2/3rd majority.
articles.plain_explanation: Establishes Supreme Court and Collegium appointment mechanism (NJAC struck down in Fourth Judges Case [2015] INSC 777).
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 124.

articles.heading: Salaries, etc., of Judges
articles.verbatim_text: Salaries and pension rights of Supreme Court Judges specified in Second Schedule.
articles.plain_explanation: Judicial salary protections.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 125.

articles.heading: Appointment of acting Chief Justice
articles.verbatim_text: President appoints senior Judge as acting CJI during vacancy.
articles.plain_explanation: Acting CJI appointment.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 126.

articles.heading: Appointment of ad hoc Judges
articles.verbatim_text: CJI with President's consent may request High Court Judge to attend SC sittings as ad hoc Judge.
articles.plain_explanation: Ad hoc SC judges.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 127.

articles.heading: Attendance of retired Judges at sittings of Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: CJI may request retired SC or HC Judge to sit and act as SC Judge.
articles.plain_explanation: Retired judges sitting.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 128.

articles.heading: Supreme Court to be a court of record
articles.verbatim_text: The Supreme Court shall be a court of record and shall have all the powers of such a court including the power to punish for contempt of itself.
articles.plain_explanation: Confers inherent power on Supreme Court to punish for civil and criminal contempt to uphold judicial majesty.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 129.

articles.heading: Seat of Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: Supreme Court sits in Delhi or such other place as CJI with President's approval may appoint.
articles.plain_explanation: Seat of the Supreme Court.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 130.

articles.heading: Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: Supreme Court has exclusive original jurisdiction in disputes between Government of India and one or more States, or between two or more States involving legal rights.
articles.plain_explanation: Exclusive federal dispute adjudication forum between Union and States.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 131.

articles.heading: Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in appeals from High Courts in certain cases
articles.verbatim_text: Appeals on substantial questions of constitutional interpretation certified by High Court under Article 134A.
articles.plain_explanation: Appellate constitutional gateway.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 132.

articles.heading: Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in appeals from High Courts in civil matters
articles.verbatim_text: Appeals on substantial questions of law of general importance certified by High Court.
articles.plain_explanation: Civil appeals to Supreme Court.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 133.

articles.heading: Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in criminal matters
articles.verbatim_text: Appeals in criminal cases where High Court reversed acquittal and sentenced to death.
articles.plain_explanation: Criminal appeals to Supreme Court.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 134.

articles.heading: Certificate for appeal to the Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: High Court determination of certificate of fitness for appeal to Supreme Court under Arts 132, 133, 134.
articles.plain_explanation: High Court certificate for appeal.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 134A.

articles.heading: Jurisdiction and powers of the Federal Court under existing law
articles.verbatim_text: Supreme Court exercises powers of pre-1950 Federal Court.
articles.plain_explanation: Transitional Federal Court powers.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 135.

articles.heading: Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything in this Chapter, the Supreme Court may, in its discretion, grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order in any cause or matter passed or made by any court or tribunal in the territory of India.
articles.plain_explanation: Plenary, discretionary extraordinary appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court against any court or tribunal in India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 136.

articles.heading: Review of judgments or orders by the Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: Subject to the provisions of any law and rules, the Supreme Court shall have power to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it.
articles.plain_explanation: Empowers Supreme Court to review its own decisions to prevent miscarriage of justice (Rupa Ashok Hurra - Curative Petitions).
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 137.

articles.heading: Enlargement of the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: Parliament may by law confer further jurisdiction with respect to Union List matters.
articles.plain_explanation: Parliamentary enlargement of SC powers.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 138.

articles.heading: Conferment on Supreme Court of powers to issue certain writs
articles.verbatim_text: Parliament may confer power to issue writs for purposes other than Part III.
articles.plain_explanation: Extension of writ powers.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 139.

articles.heading: Transfer of certain cases
articles.verbatim_text: Supreme Court may withdraw cases involving substantially same questions of general importance from High Courts to itself or transfer between High Courts.
articles.plain_explanation: Supreme Court transfer petitions.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 139A.

articles.heading: Ancillary powers of Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: Parliament may confer supplemental powers not inconsistent with Constitution.
articles.plain_explanation: Ancillary SC powers.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 140.

articles.heading: Law declared by Supreme Court to be binding on all courts
articles.verbatim_text: The law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.
articles.plain_explanation: Doctrine of Stare Decisis: every Supreme Court judgment sets authoritative binding statutory precedent for all High Courts and subordinate courts across India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 141.

articles.heading: Enforcement of decrees and orders of Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc.
articles.verbatim_text: (1) The Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it, and any decree so passed or order so made shall be enforceable throughout the territory of India.
articles.plain_explanation: Extraordinary inherent power of the Supreme Court to do complete justice, grant relief where statutory law is silent, or grant divorces on irretrievable breakdown.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 142.

articles.heading: Power of President to consult Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: President may refer questions of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for advisory opinion.
articles.plain_explanation: Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 143.

articles.heading: Civil and judicial authorities to act in aid of the Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: All authorities, civil and judicial, in the territory of India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court.
articles.plain_explanation: Mandatory all-India obedience to Supreme Court orders.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 144.

articles.heading: Rules of Court, etc.
articles.verbatim_text: Supreme Court may make rules for regulating court practice and procedure with President's approval; minimum 5 Judges for substantial constitutional interpretations.
articles.plain_explanation: Supreme Court Rules and Constitution Bench quorum.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 145.

articles.heading: Officers and servants and expenses of the Supreme Court
articles.verbatim_text: Appointments made by CJI; expenses charged on Consolidated Fund of India.
articles.plain_explanation: Supreme Court institutional independence.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 146.

articles.heading: Interpretation
articles.verbatim_text: Interpretation of Constitution and Government of India Act 1935.
articles.plain_explanation: Interpretation references.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 147.

articles.heading: Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
articles.verbatim_text: There shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India appointed by President, independent of executive, removable only like a Supreme Court Judge.
articles.plain_explanation: Establishes the independent financial watchdog of the Republic.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 148.

articles.heading: Duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
articles.verbatim_text: Performs duties and exercises powers in relation to accounts of Union and States as prescribed by law.
articles.plain_explanation: CAG statutory audit powers.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 149.

articles.heading: Form of accounts of Union and States
articles.verbatim_text: Accounts kept in form prescribed by President on advice of CAG.
articles.plain_explanation: National accounting standards.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 150.

articles.heading: Audit reports
articles.verbatim_text: CAG reports submitted to President/Governor and laid before Parliament/State Legislatures.
articles.plain_explanation: CAG tabling before Parliament.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 151.

articles.heading: Constitutional Provision regarding Article 152
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 152 of the Constitution of India regarding Constitutional Provision regarding Article 152.
articles.plain_explanation: Constitutional Provision regarding Article 152 under Part VI of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 152.

articles.heading: Governors of States
articles.verbatim_text: There shall be a Governor for each State.
articles.plain_explanation: Constitutional executive head of the State.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 153.

articles.heading: Executive power of State
articles.verbatim_text: Executive power of State vested in Governor.
articles.plain_explanation: State executive power.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 154.

articles.heading: Appointment of Governor
articles.verbatim_text: Governor appointed by President by warrant under his hand and seal.
articles.plain_explanation: Governor appointment.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 155.

articles.heading: Term of office of Governor
articles.verbatim_text: Governor holds office during pleasure of the President; 5-year normal term.
articles.plain_explanation: Governor tenure and pleasure doctrine.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 156.

articles.heading: Qualifications for appointment as Governor
articles.verbatim_text: Citizen of India, 35+ years of age.
articles.plain_explanation: Governor qualifications.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 157.

articles.heading: Conditions of Governor's office
articles.verbatim_text: Governor shall not be MP/MLA or hold office of profit.
articles.plain_explanation: Governor office conditions.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 158.

articles.heading: Oath or affirmation by the Governor
articles.verbatim_text: Solemn oath before Chief Justice of High Court to preserve, protect and defend Constitution.
articles.plain_explanation: Governor oath.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 159.

articles.heading: Discharge of functions of Governor in certain contingencies
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 160 of the Constitution of India regarding Discharge of functions of Governor in certain contingencies.
articles.plain_explanation: Discharge of functions of Governor in certain contingencies under Part VI of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 160.

articles.heading: Power of Governor to grant pardons, etc.
articles.verbatim_text: Governor power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions in State law matters.
articles.plain_explanation: Governor constitutional clemency power.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 161.

articles.heading: Extent of executive power of State
articles.verbatim_text: State executive power is co-extensive with legislative competence of State Legislature.
articles.plain_explanation: Extent of State executive power.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 162.

articles.heading: Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor
articles.verbatim_text: Council of Ministers with Chief Minister at head to aid and advise Governor, except in matters where Governor acts in his discretion under the Constitution.
articles.plain_explanation: Establishes Cabinet governance in States; discretionary powers are exceptional and judicially reviewable (Nabam Rebia).
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 163.

articles.heading: Other provisions as to Ministers
articles.verbatim_text: Chief Minister appointed by Governor; other Ministers appointed on CM advice; collective responsibility to Legislative Assembly.
articles.plain_explanation: Cabinet appointment and collective responsibility in States.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 164.

articles.heading: Advocate-General for the State
articles.verbatim_text: Governor shall appoint a person qualified to be High Court Judge as Advocate-General to advise State Government.
articles.plain_explanation: Highest law officer of the State Government.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 165.

articles.heading: Conduct of business of the Government of a State
articles.verbatim_text: All executive action expressed to be taken in name of Governor; authentication rules.
articles.plain_explanation: State executive orders authentication.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 166.

articles.heading: Duties of Chief Minister as respects furnishing of information to Governor
articles.verbatim_text: CM duty to communicate all Cabinet decisions and legislative proposals to Governor.
articles.plain_explanation: CM reporting duty to Governor.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 167.

articles.heading: Constitution of Legislatures in States
articles.verbatim_text: Legislatures consist of Governor and one or two Houses (Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council).
articles.plain_explanation: State legislature structures.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 168.

articles.heading: Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States
articles.verbatim_text: Parliament may by law abolish or create Legislative Council if State Assembly passes resolution by 2/3rd majority.
articles.plain_explanation: Creation/abolition of Vidhan Parishads.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 169.

articles.heading: Composition of the Legislative Assemblies
articles.verbatim_text: State Legislative Assembly consists of 60 to 500 members chosen by direct election.
articles.plain_explanation: State Assembly composition.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 170.

articles.heading: Composition of the Legislative Councils
articles.verbatim_text: Legislative Council membership capped at 1/3rd of Assembly; elected by local bodies, graduates, teachers, and Governor nominations.
articles.plain_explanation: State Legislative Council composition.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 171.

articles.heading: Duration of State Legislatures
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 172 of the Constitution of India regarding Duration of State Legislatures.
articles.plain_explanation: Duration of State Legislatures under Part VI of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 172.

articles.heading: Qualification for membership of State Legislature
articles.verbatim_text: Official gazetted text of Article 173 of the Constitution of India regarding Qualification for membership of State Legislature.
articles.plain_explanation: Qualification for membership of State Legislature under Part VI of the Constitution of India.
articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Plead statutory violation and seek constitutional enforcement under Article 173.

articles.heading: Sessions of State Legislature, prorogation and dissolution
articles.verbatim_text: Governor summons, prorogues, and dissolves Legislative Assembly.

articles.heading: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor
articles.verbatim_text: (1) Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article. (2) Bill must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership and by a majority of not less than 2/3rd members present and voting. Federal provisions require 50% State ratification.
articles.plain_explanation: Constituent amending power of Parliament, bounded by the immortal Basic Structure Doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati, Minerva Mills).
applicable_doctrines: Limited Amending Power Cannot Expand Itself

landmark_precedents.case_title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Parliament has wide power to amend any provision of the Constitution under Article 368, but cannot alter, damage, or destroy the basic structure or essential framework of the Constitution.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Basic Structure Doctrine as Supreme Constitutional Limitation

landmark_precedents.case_title: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India
landmark_precedents.ratio_decidendi: Clause (4) and (5) of Article 368 seeking to confer unlimited amending power struck down; limited amending power is itself a basic structure feature.
landmark_precedents.doctrine_established: Inviolability of Constitutional Checks on Amending Power

articles.advocate_pleading_notes: Every constitutional amendment challenge tests whether the amendment destroys secularism, judicial review, federalism, free elections, or equality.
citizen_actionable_rights: Ultimate sovereign guarantee that the democratic, secular, federal, and fundamental rights foundation of India can never be subverted by any parliamentary majority.
